title: The か particle
summary: か turns a statement into a question-like idea that can sit inside another sentence: whether, or, maybe, I wonder, as if. It is always uncertain, never a confirmed fact.

blocks.text: At the end of a polite sentence **か** marks a question. In casual speech tone does that job. But か does much of its work **inside** sentences, and every use grows from one function: **it turns a proposition into an uncertain, question-like thing**.
Place か after a clause and it becomes a noun-like "whether ...", which can be the object of 分からない, 知っている and so on. Usually no が or を is added after か.

blocks.jp: さくらが来るか分からない。
blocks.en: I do not know whether Sakura will come.

blocks.jp: これは誰の本か分かりますか。
blocks.en: Do you know whose book this is?

blocks.text: **かどうか** spells out "or not": 来るかどうか分からない.

rows: か + も + しれない

blocks.en: I wonder if it will rain tomorrow.

blocks.jp: そんな物を食べるもんか。
blocks.en: As if I would eat such a thing!

blocks.jp: 漢字どころか、ひらがなも読めない。
blocks.en: Far from kanji, I cannot even read hiragana.

blocks.text: As in lesson 26, か marks a situation as imagined, not real: ゆうれいを見た**か**のような顔, "a face as if she had seen a ghost".

items: **Clause + か + 分からない / 知らない**: whether ...
**か + どうか**: whether or not.
**A か B**: A or B; **かもしれない**: might; **かな**: I wonder.
**ものか / もんか**: strong rhetorical denial.
